purpose: Keep candidate admission, field scoring and diagnostic evidence consistent while recovering document-level context across section boundaries.

matching.normalization: Core uses locale-independent Unicode NFC and full case folding from pinned utf8proc 2.12.0. Letters and numbers are searchable across scripts; combining marks remain attached to a preceding word. ASCII identifier boundaries and scoring are preserved. Invalid UTF-8 bytes become separators, never joined letters.
matching.exact: Exact terms and identifiers retain higher evidence than broad partial matches.
matching.prefix: Prefix completion is bounded, counts at least four Unicode letters/numbers rather than bytes, and is used only where the query form permits it.

nativeSourceQuery.scope: Native source_context and explicit source discovery. These query hints do not redefine Core query-group coverage, evidence authority or source permissions; Core Unicode normalization is specified separately.
nativeSourceQuery.terms: Tokenize the original query with unicode61. Remove EN/RU question stop words only from multi-token queries. Keep original meaningful terms; add bounded English hints for reviewed Russian software concepts and inflections from src/source_query_terms.cpp. No repository names, source paths, known-answer symbols, external translation service or model are part of this lexicon.
nativeSourceQuery.matching: The source index retains raw source text and CamelCase components under the built-in Porter/unicode61 tokenizer. Porter normalizes English forms; it is not a Russian stemmer. Deduplicate query terms by their actual indexed stem before OR matching, so multiple inflections do not multiply BM25 weight. Keep one original term as each stem's representative; do not stem an already-stemmed string again.
nativeSourceQuery.bounds: At most 4096 query bytes, 64 distinct unicode61 vocabulary terms and 256 expanded terms. Native service admission and standalone discovery apply the same term budget before reader preparation. Over-budget queries return source-discovery-token-limit with guidance to split or narrow the query. Repeated spellings that normalize to one term share a slot. Source/chunk/time, eight-result, two-per-file and source-view byte limits still apply. Quoted tokens cannot introduce FTS operators.
nativeSourceQuery.cache: The derived source cache uses shin.source-cache.v3; older tokenizer/projection caches rebuild through normal preparation. Temporary vocabulary tables are excluded from cache serialization, including candidate-to-publication transfer after a query. Query calls do not persist cache changes. Cleanup recognizes v2 and v3 only with their corresponding exact table set and existing project/index ownership checks; unknown or mismatched contents remain preserved.
nativeSourceQuery.limits: This finite software vocabulary is not general sentence translation or semantic search. Unknown words remain literal, ambiguous concepts may retrieve several owners, and valid fresh locators do not prove relevance or answer completeness. Source code, tests and contracts compete without hard-coded path boosts.
nativeSourceQuery.verification: tests/core/source_discovery_test.cpp covers EN/RU descriptions, literal Cyrillic, exact identifiers, unknown/stop-word negatives, equal inflection weights, broad-query file diversity and spare-span filling, cold/restored parity, cache-format replacement, transfer query privacy, source identity and redaction. Compare frozen native MCP cohorts separately from hermetic correctness gates.
nativeSourceQuery.selection: Queries with at least four distinct original non-stop vocabulary terms first select the best BM25 span from different files. Second spans fill spare capacity in BM25 order. Short queries retain ordinary span order. Translation expansions do not activate this policy. The result reports distinct_paths_first; this is a lexical heuristic, not inferred task intent.

compoundBriefRetention.activation: During fallback for queries with at least eight term groups, a bounded row matching every query group retains priority over partial rows when candidates compete for retention or selection. Matches using a Markdown indexed_text body keep ordinary scoring, so incidental prose cannot suppress focused headings.
compoundBriefRetention.scope: Ordinary generated-index and source-scan Brief, including document-planner evidence; explicit owner and first-term scope routes keep their existing policies.
compoundBriefRetention.boundary: Explicit lifecycle/authority penalties prevent this priority. Field scores, candidate admission, row provenance, type diversity, per-document limits and output budgets remain unchanged. Additional partial evidence remains eligible; a full match is lexical support, not proof of a complete answer.

sparseBriefSupplement.activation: For ordinary indexed Brief queries with four to seven term groups and one strict document, bounded majority-coverage supplementation also applies when the full match depends on indexed_text beyond the compact preview and fewer than half the query groups match primary non-body fields. An incidental heading or filename word alone does not focus that full-text match. This incidental-primary-field supplement is accepted only when the selected leading document changes; otherwise the strict full match and compact Pack size are preserved. The existing indexed-body-only supplement is unchanged.
sparseBriefSupplement.boundary: Compact full matches with non-body support, majority primary-field matches, explicit status/authority/record-type qualifiers, independent facts, multiple strict owners and explicit owner/identifier routes keep their existing behavior. Candidate completeness, the existing indexed-row cap, scoring, provenance, per-document and output limits remain unchanged. Supplementary rows retain their actual matched groups, without borrowing missing terms.
sparseBriefSupplement.verification: tests/fixtures/lexical-retrieval/test_lexical_retrieval.py covers heading/filename distractors, focused and minority controls, strict eval variants, Pack evidence and output bounds.

narrowedFallback.activation: Before ordinary indexed Brief falls back to its relaxed threshold, try at most two posting intersections: halfway between strict and relaxed group counts, then one above the ordinary relaxed threshold. Equal thresholds are not repeated. These are optional bounded probes; incomplete or oversized postings keep the ordinary route.
narrowedFallback.acceptance: Final selected evidence must span at least two paths and cover every query group with nonempty complete postings. Narrow only when the ordinary admitted set exceeds the requested result limit; small result sets keep their complementary owners. Preserve ordinary section and independent-fact families. After narrowing, queries below eight groups also supplement declared documents using the narrowed admission threshold across their sections; an individual supplementary document need not match every query group. Compound queries retain their complete observed-coverage supplement. The final combined selected coverage must not decrease. Lexical coverage is not answer completeness; selected-evidence regression assertions remain necessary.
narrowedFallback.boundary: No query rewriting, repository-specific terms, field-score change, new output allowance or relaxed quality/resource gate. Source-scan Brief and explicit owner/directory/identifier routes retain their existing policies. Posting admission is narrower; reported candidate and scored-match counters still describe actual admitted work rather than final output size.
narrowedFallback.verification: Neutral common-pair noise and low-overlap complement scenarios join existing complete-JSON, independent-fact, document-corroboration and sparse-body controls in tests/fixtures/lexical-retrieval/test_lexical_retrieval.py.

ownerQualifierAdmission.policy: For an explicit owner with topical qualifiers, check primary lexical fields and allowed evidence types before scoring rows. When qualifying permitted evidence exists, unrelated owner-only rows do not reach scoring. Otherwise preserve the existing owner-entry fallback, including typed-only requests and unknown qualifiers.
ownerQualifierAdmission.diagnostics: candidate_rows retains the complete bounded sparse owner-probe row count. matched_sections and matched_facts count positive scored matches after qualifier admission; no discovery work is relabelled as returned evidence.
ownerQualifierAdmission.verification: An owner with eighty unrelated sections still returns both topical sections, keeps actual group coverage and reports all probed rows; existing lifecycle, allowed-type and entry-fallback scenarios remain required.

jsonKeyPolicy.scanner: JsonKeySpan is an O(n), line-oriented lexical-balanced scanner. A key span includes its own scalar value line or balanced container subtree and ends on the matching close line; subsequent sibling lines are not appended.
jsonKeyPolicy.strings: Quoted braces and escaped quotes are ignored while balancing delimiters, so braces inside JSON strings cannot close a container early.
jsonKeyPolicy.boundary: The span extractor is line-oriented range extraction, not full JSON validation or column-precise AST ownership. Multiple members sharing a line remain line-granular. It makes no malformed-JSON validation claim.

sectionPublication.registeredFormats: Explicitly enrolled .mdc documents use the existing Markdown pipeline, case-insensitively, with original paths and ranges. Profiles own enrollment; hidden directories are not discovered implicitly. globs and alwaysApply remain client metadata, not executed policy or authority. Earlier publications require rebuilding with the current generator; evidence row shapes remain unchanged.
sectionPublication.shape: Existing Markdown section, chunk and document rows retain their original ranges. indexed_text is the normalized, redacted body, separate from the compact preview; no new paragraph rows are introduced.
sectionPublication.matching: Nonempty indexed_text replaces preview in the shared publication/scoring projection at weight 16. Empty fields retain preview matching. Selection policy is documented separately in documentCandidates.
sectionPublication.allocation: Allocate in existing source row order, including overlapping sections/chunks. Redact the complete body before whitespace-boundary clipping, preserving UTF-8 and whole tokens.
sectionPublication.omission: indexed_text_omitted_bytes counts normalized redacted bytes omitted from this field, saturated at INT_MAX. It is not a raw-source byte count or coverage by other records. JSON sections publish empty text and zero omissions.
sectionPublication.identity: Search-only text and omissions participate in typed equality, independent retrieval-unit keys, deterministic ordering and full canonical Pack identity before display projection. Resident and disk readers use the same strict decoder.

retrievalUnits.declaration: The verified manifest sources array declares document kind. Only markdown and json documents permit whole-document corroboration. JSONL rows and source-fact records are independent units; extension guessing or consumer vocabulary is not used.
retrievalUnits.identity: Whole-document units are separated by path, evidence_kind, verification_level, authority_level and status. Independent units additionally retain exact decoded record content, origin and ranges, including SectionRow indexed_text and indexed_text_omitted_bytes. Equal previews never authorize merging distinct independent searchable records. Source facts remain independent even when their physical path is also enrolled as a document.
retrievalUnits.factDeduplication: FactRow uses C++20 defaulted field-by-field comparison for exact deduplication, without serializing lookup keys. Exact decoded copies can merge; differing paths, ranges, origins, statuses, authority or contents cannot. A generic fact with an explicit source and its lossy typed projection are not exact copies and remain distinct candidates. Final output budgets still apply.
retrievalUnits.admission: Document posting preselection may combine section/typed-record groups for declared whole documents, never independent facts or JSONL records. A sparse plan may qualify document group coverage before merging and scoring rows only when every originally available posting group remains represented. Otherwise retain the distributed partial-document route; common-term cap recovery also keeps its existing policy. Independent records remain eligible as separate units with only their own groups; they never inherit document corroboration. Exact decoded scoring and unit checks follow this conservative preselection.
retrievalUnits.selection: Sparse planning selects bounded units and respects per-document limits. A source unit contributes only its own matched groups. Planner acceptance is checked against final selected coverage, not coverage of discarded records. For compound queries with at least eight groups and multiple strict owners, a full ordinary row budget still permits bounded supplementation by complete document units; shorter queries retain their spare-budget rule.
retrievalUnits.corroboration: A document unit may contribute corroborating group paths only when a representative of that exact provenance/status/authority unit survives final selection. Another record at the same physical path does not authorize it.
retrievalUnits.boundary: This is an explicit structural retrieval scope, not a compiler call graph or semantic relevance guarantee. No field weights, consumer policies or generated snapshot format change in this correction.
retrievalUnits.nearCompleteHeadingCorroboration: When the existing multi-document body-only supplement is eligible, a section missing one query group may use a non-body match from a sibling section of the same declared document unit. Filename-only matches, independent rows, differing status/authority/provenance and fabricated coverage remain excluded. Indexed candidate and output limits remain unchanged.
retrievalUnits.broadGroupRecovery: An individual common-term row cutoff does not establish incomplete lexical coverage. Recover ordinary intersections under the existing cap; for document planning read complete postings one group at a time, exclude independent facts, qualify declared document owners before retaining candidates, and enforce the existing candidate union and output caps. Incomplete postings still refuse. A genuinely oversized final candidate set reports document-candidate-budget-exceeded; profiles and project quality gates remain unchanged.

diagnostics.matching: Includes policy, independent-expected-path-probe-not-selection scope and document_matched_groups. A path-local score is not a declaration of candidate admission or selection.
diagnostics.ordinary_row_candidate_probe: Reports strict and relaxed posting-stage candidate counts, expected-path admitted row counts and sparse path-probe completeness. When the ordinary clause uses a generated-row scan, admitted rows are unknown/null, not zero. This probe is separate from owner, identifier and document-planner selection.

verification.boundary: These contracts do not promise semantic understanding, runtime truth, or ranking quality on an unmeasured corpus.

compactLexicalCandidate.compatibility: current generator only; rebuild previous indexes

prefixCompletion.activation: Disabled for ordinary public query construction. Query length never changes exact lexical terms into prefix matches.
prefixCompletion.boundary: Internal opt-in prefix matching helpers remain bounded; no public autocomplete mode is introduced by this candidate.

fastPrefilter.policy: A necessary ASCII subsequence check and positive lexical word-boundary shortcut may avoid vocabulary allocation. They do not change the canonical lexical match predicate.
fastPrefilter.nativePropertyTest: Core 2.0 assert_lexical_word_match_equivalence compares field matching to indexed vocabulary, including camel boundaries, punctuation and numeric terms. The obsolete atomic-source matcher was removed.

previewRedaction.policy: Redact complete normalized lines before joining, and complete collected preview/summary values before truncation. JSON, JSONL and source declarations follow the same order.
previewRedaction.boundary: This preserves the existing heuristic detector, not a claim that every secret is recognized. It prevents clipping a recognizable credential into a sensitive unrecognizable prefix and keeps assignment detection within its original line boundary.
previewRedaction.verification: Synthetic credential controls cover 280/420/900-byte cutoffs, assignment line boundaries, JSON/JSONL summaries and source declarations.

coverage.rows: matched_group_indices describe that exact returned row, including explicitly marked prefix support; rows never inherit other sections' matches.
coverage.documents: selected_document_paths may describe corroborating rows within the same returned whole-document unit. Paths from discarded units, independent source members, JSONL records or different provenance/status/authority are not credited merely because the physical path survives.
coverage.boundary: Document coverage is lexical retrieval evidence, not semantic completeness, correctness, execution proof or a compiler-resolved dependency.

sourceCorpus.implementation: src/generation.cpp: build_source_scan_corpus reuses build_generated_rows without serialization or publication.
sourceCorpus.projection: src/extraction.cpp: query_fact_row projects decisions and typed references into the same fields as generated-row decoding.
sourceCorpus.invariant: On the same corpus and row threshold, indexed Context and source-scan Context return identical scored sections/facts, source ranges, provenance, match groups and match counts.
sourceCorpus.boundary: This invariant does not equate Brief owner/planner routing with source-scan Brief or legacy raw-line source-scan Search. Those modes are explicit and never an implicit fallback from a corrupt or stale snapshot.

unicodePublication.compatibility: One current reader/writer. Older generator retrieval is rejected; there is no legacy JSONL/TSV term reader or writer. Raw prior manifest integrity/ownership may be inspected only to authorize rebuilding from current approved sources.
unicodePublication.rebuild: The normal granted or bootstrap publisher detects generator drift, qualifies a fresh candidate and atomically publishes it. No old lexical data conversion, manual index repair, grant takeover or history deletion. Failed preparation preserves the current publication and reports the failure. Standalone Core requires an explicit build.
unicodePublication.coverage: Request terms, profile aliases, generated keys, full-text matching and disk/resident readers share normalization. Original paths, source bytes, hashes, line ranges and provenance remain unchanged. Unicode support does not translate queries, strip accents, equate visually confusable scripts or segment arbitrary natural-language sentences.
unicodePublication.limits: Existing 128-byte lexical keys, candidate ceilings, output limits and source boundaries remain in force. Non-ASCII single-letter terms can be meaningful; prefix completion still requires four letters/numbers.

executionPlan.owner: One request-owned RetrievalPlan records owner, directory, identifier, strict, supplement, narrowed, relaxed, planner and document-relation attempts, including rejected work. It is shared by Brief, Eval, Diagnose and Pack retrieval.
executionPlan.cost: query_plan reports cumulative candidate-row visits and positive section/fact score visits, counting repeat visits. Existing candidate counters still describe the chosen stage. Optional work is admitted against a fixed eight-times-indexed-row-cap budget and a bounded stage list; mandatory ordinary fallback remains available. Counts are not elapsed time, posting I/O, unique rows or a relevance verdict. Detailed query_plan appears in full Brief and Eval, while compact agent delivery omits internal stage counters.
executionPlan.selection: Narrowing never removes an otherwise fitting small complementary set. Final record, per-document, evidence-type, provenance and output budgets remain authoritative.
executionPlan.shortQueryScoring: Below eight groups, complete postings may admit missing document units before scoring narrowed rows. A combined pass is accepted only with at least two returned paths and final coverage of every group with nonempty complete postings. It scores the ordinary candidates once, not once before and again inside the planner. A rejected plan keeps the ordinary fallback, rejected diagnostics and optional-work ceiling; compound-query supplementation retains its existing policy.

documentLifecycle.metadata: Within the 64-line preamble before the first section or code fence, recognize ordinary Supersedes, Superseded by, Amends and Amended by declarations, with optional colons, wrapped link lists, and explicit partial-subject reverse prose. Status preambles may include an amendment sentence; accepted/active/approved/implemented status may carry a date or explanatory suffix. Only enrolled, nonquarantined Markdown endpoints qualify. Drafts cannot retire accepted evidence.
documentLifecycle.scope: Only a bare document-level Supersedes/Superseded by declaration can mark older declared sections and typed records superseded/history. An old-target anchor limits retirement to that section range. Named-concern prose records a partial relation and retains the other operative rules; Amends always retains both. Implementation-source facts, source bytes and declared document metadata are unchanged. Section dispositions also cover their generated chunks. Effective historical status carries the declaration/current-owner verification dependencies even if its explanatory notice is outside the view budget.
documentLifecycle.uncertainty: Cycles remain ambiguous. At most 1024 relations are retained; omissions disable automatic retirement and are reported. Unconfirmed relations remain explicit notices. Ordinary prose or examples do not authorize retirement.
documentLifecycle.delivery: At most four related newer owners are considered under shared optional work and output caps. Partial amendments retain ordinary evidence families and ranks, filling spare space only; saturated results carry notices without speculative retrieval. Whole replacements can prioritize current evidence while an explicit owner request retains its named owner. Original groups are rescored without borrowing the owner lookup term; score_components documents relation priority. Notices retain at most eight whole records and 4096 bytes, with separate relation/inventory omission counts. A notice does not prove a companion body was delivered. Declarations and endpoints participate in selected-source verification; retained partial delivery withholds affected evidence if declarations cannot be verified.
documentLifecycle.limits: Relations qualify declared evidence; they do not prove implementation or infer the meaning of arbitrary prose. No archive layout, project-specific path boost or consumer vocabulary is required.
